criteria.opaque_with_constructors: Introduce an opaque type for each closed set in compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json, together with one no-argument constructor operation per member: 4 for make_kind, 7 for observe_kind, 3 for hostile_descriptor, 5 for read_op (19 constructors total), each returning its opaque type. Callers can then only obtain a member through its constructor, which makes it impossible for an arbitrary string to reach a closed parameter. The 7 sets lacking authoritative tables remain plain str. Every constructor requires checker admission and an emitter lowering, so any TS table change must land together with the matching constructor change.
criteria.str_with_checker_allowlist: Keep every closed-set parameter as str in compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json and put membership enforcement in the new NT-I01 checker admission module, mirroring the checkBrowserTag approach from compiler/internal/check/browser.go: the module carries copies of the four authoritative tables (NATIVE_MAKE_KINDS with 4 members, NATIVE_OBSERVE_KINDS with 7 members, NATIVE_HOSTILE_DESCRIPTORS with 3 members, NATIVE_READ_OPS with 5 members), demands a string literal for each closed-set argument, and rejects literals outside the table with exact-match comparison. The 7 sets without tables (fault_mode, registered_runtime, registered_api, registered_operation, reviewed_fault_target, observer_id, scope_ref) remain plain str with membership governed by review and documented as such. The 9-member observe_kind note is recorded as drift against the authoritative 7-member const and filed as a K-lane finding.
criteria.variant_unit_leaves: Express the 4 table-backed sets as Can variants in compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json, giving each member its own unit leaf type: 4 leaves for make_kind, 7 for observe_kind, 3 for hostile_descriptor, 5 for read_op (19 leaf types total). Membership is then decided by the type checker alone and no literal inspection is needed. The 7 sets without authoritative tables remain plain str. Each leaf type needs emitter support for lowering to its wire string, and TS table edits must be paired with matching leaf changes.

closed_set_modeling.instructions: For the native-values merge, which representation of the closed string sets keeps the contract strongest while adding the smallest hidden surface?

state: Task I01 wires the native-values service contracts (tools/runtime/test-services/native-values/schema.ts, session.ts, observe.ts) into Can through compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json and a new NT-I01 checker admission module. Pre-dispatch, the services recognize closed string sets at two assurance levels. Level A sets are enforced at runtime by const tables plus includes() validation: session.ts defines NATIVE_MAKE_KINDS (primitive_bits, text, ordered_entries, hostile_descriptor) and NATIVE_HOSTILE_DESCRIPTORS (getter_then, throwing_thenable, revoked_proxy); observe.ts defines NATIVE_OBSERVE_KINDS (scalar_tag, ieee_bits, lexeme, descriptor, entries, identity, counters) and NATIVE_READ_OPS (bits, text, entries, property_then, call_then). Level B sets are enforced nowhere in code: fault_mode is named only by a schema.ts catalogue note (absent, throw, revoked, counted_delegate) with no backing const; registered_runtime, registered_api, registered_operation and reviewed_fault_target have no member lists anywhere; observer_id and scope_ref accept any ID-pattern string. Verified drift: the schema.ts observe_kind note advertises 9 members (bytes and events extra) but NATIVE_OBSERVE_KINDS contains 7, and the const wins. Fixed limits: catalogue.json offers no enum kind and drops unknown fields via DisallowUnknownFields (so the proposal nativeTest block goes); a variant costs one type leaf per member; an opaque type with no constructor is unbuildable from Can; static string literals are readable by the checker (checkBrowserTag in compiler/internal/check/browser.go), whereas the I04 http_peer precedent left constrained strings open; mechanism must carry closedness, not names.
